Guidance for Claude Code (claude.ai/code): This is an MCP server delivering Go updates and best practices as structured Markdown. Current version v0.2.0; supports Go 1.13–1.24 (12 versions). Clean architecture; Go 1.24 practices.

Commands:
`go build -o recent-go-mcp` - Build server
`go test ./...` - Run all tests
`go test -v -run TestMCPServer` - Run MCP integration tests
`go mod tidy` - Clean dependencies
`go fmt ./...` - Format
`go vet ./...` - Static analysis

Protocol checks:
`echo '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list"}' | ./recent-go-mcp`
`echo '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "go-updates", "arguments": {"version": "1.24"}}}' | ./recent-go-mcp`
`echo '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "go-updates", "arguments": {"version": "1.22", "package": "slices"}}}' | ./recent-go-mcp`

Architecture: `main.go` hosts MCP server, `NewMCPServer()` factory and version constants; `internal/domain/` models, interfaces, structured errors; `internal/service/` business logic/context; `internal/storage/` embedded data; `internal/version/` comparison via Go 1.22+ `go/version`; `data/releases/` JSON for Go 1.13–1.24, embedded via `//go:embed` in main.go. Uses dependency injection, repository pattern (`ReleaseRepository`), clean architecture, SOLID principles, MCP protocol.

Add releases: create `data/releases/go{version}.json` in existing structure (version, changes, package updates). Embedded repository automatically discovers and loads all `.json` files in the releases directory; no code changes required. Sorting/comparison automatic. Releases sorted newest-first; changes categorized "new", "enhancement", "performance", "breaking", "deprecation".

Testing includes MCP client-server tests with `NewInProcessClient`, mocked unit tests, version comparator tests, and service/repository tests.

Single tool `go-updates`: required Go version (e.g. "1.21"–"1.24"), optional package filter (e.g. "net/http", "slices", "maps"), structured Markdown output with examples, impact indicators, upgrade recommendations, and modern features (`slices`, `maps`, `log/slog`, `go/version`). Output is ~70% smaller than prior dual-format approach.

Practices shown: wrapped structured errors, `context.Context` propagation, `slices.SortFunc`/`Clone`/`IndexFunc`, `strings.Builder`, JSON `log/slog`, `go/version.Compare`, interfaces for testability.
